summary: The fsgg-coord shim's documented four-tier engine resolution let a one-line tool-manifest bump be verified as a controlled experiment rather than asserted, and made the mid-wave bump provably invisible to five concurrent lanes before merge.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord --version (0.71.0.0 before the edit, 0.72.0.0 after, same tree and same shell env); command:printenv FSGG_COORD_ENGINE_BIN -> unset (tier 1 absent); command:command -v fsgg-coord-engine -> not found (tier 3 absent); command:ls -d src/FS.GG.Coord.Cli -> absent (tier 2 absent), so tier 4 .config/dotnet-tools.json is the sole resolver; file:.config/dotnet-tools.json

summary: The worktree-isolation guard refused four non-git commands and named git as the cause, so the diagnostic pointed away from the real constraint (compound shell syntax) and cost four retries.
evidence: command:dotnet tool restore piped to tail with a trailing PIPESTATUS echo -> refused with 'a worktree-isolated agent git operations must target its own worktree'; command:printenv FSGG_COORD_ENGINE_BIN combined with ls -d in one line -> same refusal; the identical commands split into single statements ran unchanged and stayed inside the worktree
cost: four avoidable retries; roughly six tool calls spent re-splitting commands that were never git operations
owner: agent harness worktree-isolation guard (outside FS-GG repos); same wrong-cause diagnostic class as EHotwagner/S.I.R.#256

summary: A host disposition pinned a version on a release-channel fact that was already six minutes stale when written, and nothing between the disposition and implementation re-read the channel, so the item would have shipped the second-newest promoted stable release while calling itself currency hygiene.
evidence: command:gh release view coherent-set/v0.73.1 --repo FS-GG/.github --json name,isDraft,isPrerelease,publishedAt,tagName -> isDraft false, publishedAt 2026-08-22T20:07:33Z, no (publishing) suffix; command:gh release download coherent-set/v0.73.1 --repo FS-GG/.github --pattern stable-channel.json --output - -> version 0.73.1 promotedAt 2026-08-22T20:07:30Z, against 0.72.0 promotedAt 2026-08-22T11:17:06Z; issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#250
cost: no rework to the diff; one board round-trip to raise the boundary question, and the item is held pending a host decision it could otherwise have been given up front
owner: work-board host disposition step; a channel fact quoted as a merge-blocking reason needs re-reading at claim time rather than at disposition time

summary: The review-wait entry that gates critic dispatch is undocumented in every packed skill, and three of its four non-obvious field rules can only be learned by reflecting on the engine assembly or by reading successive fail-closed refusals.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord review S.I.R.#250 --pr 257 --json -> noVerdict, 'dispatchCritic requires a durable review-wait entry before dispatch'; command:dotnet fsi over FS.GG.Coord.Core.dll reflecting FS.GG.Coord.ReviewWait -> WaitReceipt fields Item, ClaimGeneration, ReviewGeneration, Kind, EnteredAt, ExpiresAt, EvidenceRef and statics validate/encode/generationToken/tryDecode/project; issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#255
cost: three refused attempts before the entry was accepted, plus one wrong-round entry that had to be cancelled and re-entered
owner: EHotwagner/S.I.R. packed independent-review contract in the .claude, .agents and .codex skill mirrors; already scoped as S.I.R.#255 and not re-filed

summary: Two concurrent item lanes were given the same scratchpad directory and independently chose the same obvious filenames for their review-wait helper scripts and event payloads, so each silently overwrote the other mid-task.
evidence: Three of this lane's scratchpad files (reflect.fsx, reflect2.fsx, mkwait.fsx) were replaced in place by another lane's versions pinned to fs.gg.coord.cli 0.71.0 and targeting EHotwagner/S.I.R.#252 and PR #254; that lane's mkwait.fsx writes to scratchpad/wait-enter.json, the exact path this lane passed to review wait; command:scripts/fsgg-coord review wait S.I.R.#250 <file> --pr 257 --json -> returned item EHotwagner/S.I.R.#250, confirming this lane's own payload was the one submitted
cost: no incorrect write occurred, because the engine validates item, claimGeneration and head and refused both mismatched probes; cost was re-verifying every helper script before reuse
owner: work-board host lane dispatch: per-lane scratchpad isolation, or a worker-id-qualified filename convention; the engine's fail-closed validation is what contained this, not the filesystem
